name: Mattaniah
overview: Mattaniah was a male Levite, specifically a Gershonite, descended from Asaph, a notable figure associated with temple music and worship. As a member of the tribe of Levi, he belonged to the family of Gershon, the son of Levi, which held particular responsibilities in the service of the tabernacle and temple. His lineage highlights his role within the Levitical order during the time of temple worship.
namesAndTitles: The name Mattaniah means "gift of YHWH," reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's providence. This proper name is recorded in 2 Chronicles 29:13 and does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a significant meaning in the Hebrew context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Mattaniah as a descendant of Asaph (2 Chronicles 29:13). It is inferred that his father was Shemaiah and his son was Micaiah, as noted in Nehemiah 12:35. These relationships place him within a lineage connected to temple musicians and Levites serving in Jerusalem.
scriptureSignificance: Mattaniah's importance rests in his Levitical heritage and connection to Asaph, a key figure in Israel's worship tradition. As a Gershonite Levite, he would have been involved in the sacred duties assigned to his clan, contributing to the maintenance and service of the temple. His presence in the biblical record underscores the continuity of Levitical families dedicated to worship and temple service during the post-exilic period.
